a: Yes. Any session can be held by Zoom with private breakout rooms for caucus and a waiting room, and I offer a short tech check the week before for anyone who wants one. In-person sessions are at 9 SW Pack Square in Asheville. Sessions are never recorded, in either format.
In person, I mediate in Buncombe County and the surrounding counties of Western North Carolina. By Zoom, I take matters statewide.

q: What should we send before the conference?
a: A short mediation summary by email, five business days before the session: the parties, the claims and defenses, procedural posture, the key documents, and any prior offers you want me to know about. Nothing confidential goes in the booking form.
Equal shares among the parties unless the court orders otherwise or counsel agree to a different split. Each party pays its own share on the Payments page and receives its own receipt.

q: What if the case settles before the conference?
a: Tell me as soon as you know and I will file the Report of Mediator. The postponement and cancellation terms apply to late notice.

q: Joint session or straight to caucus?
a: I open with a short joint session unless counsel agree otherwise, then move to private caucus. If you would rather skip the joint session, say so in the booking notes.

Yes. When a date is requested, I check every listed party, counsel and insurer against my current and former matters before confirming. If there is a conflict, I tell all counsel the same day and release the date.

q: How do we request accommodations or an interpreter?
a: Note it in the booking form or email me. The suite has an elevator and an accessible entrance; interpreters are arranged by the party who needs one. If a party needs a trauma-informed setup, such as separate arrival times or a quiet room, tell me in advance and I will plan the day around it.
